name: Vacuum cleaner fragrance additives
anchor: route-scoped sovereign inhaled-product content maxima. Lead, cadmium, total arsenic and total mercury read across from the Colorado Marijuana Enforcement Division 2022 route table for "inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray" (500 / 200 / 200 / 100 ug/kg), corroborated at identical values by California DCC section 15723 for inhalable products; total chromium reads across from the Maryland Cannabis Administration inhalation-route value (600 ug/kg) and is published as a screen. The only sovereign heavy-metal instrument in any jurisdiction that names a product in this category is the United States CPSC prohibition on lead-cored candlewicks, 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13), mirrored by Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956; it is a component prohibition on the metal of a wick core and is carried on the scented-candles row as an independent regulatory hard stop, never as a finished-article ceiling. Nickel, tin, aluminium, inorganic arsenic and hexavalent chromium are held under mandatory control because no government sets a content maximum for them in any inhaled consumer product.
native_basis_label: as sold, micrograms of element per kilogram of the emitting material (the fragrance concentrate, wax, gel, botanical mass or refill charge that is aerosolised, evaporated or combusted), with component-level screening of the article's non-emitting parts; a content screen on the article and its refill, never an emission rate, a per-actuation dose or an indoor-air concentration
scope_note: FORM AND EMISSION MECHANISM. A granule, powder, bead, disc or impregnated pad is placed in the bag, canister, filter housing or a dedicated holder, and the appliance's own airflow strips fragrance from it and discharges it through the exhaust. The exhaust of a domestic vacuum cleaner is a high-velocity jet directed into the room at floor level, so the additive is dispersed by a mechanism its manufacturer neither controls nor filters, and any friable carrier can be carried over as particulate. SCOPE. In scope: granules, powders, beads, discs, tablets, pads and impregnated strips sold to scent the exhaust of a domestic vacuum cleaner, together with any sachet or dispenser. Out of scope: carpet deodorising powders applied to the floor and vacuumed up, whose primary exposure is deposition and contact rather than exhaust emission, vacuum bags and filters with no fragrance claim, and antimicrobial or biocidal filter treatments. COMPONENTS SAMPLED. The component-level sampling plan for this row covers the carrier granule, bead, powder or pad substrate (mineral, zeolite, cellulose, starch or polymer); the fragrance load; the dye; any anti-caking, free-flow or fixative agent; and the sachet, disc backing or dispenser body. BASIS, AND WHAT THIS ROW DOES NOT MEASURE. The panel is a CONTENT SCREEN on the article and on its refill, expressed in micrograms of element per kilogram of the emitting material. It is not an inhalation exposure limit, not an emission-rate limit, not a per-actuation or per-hour dose limit, and not an indoor-air concentration limit, and it must not be presented as any of those. No credible sovereign government sets an inhalation exposure limit for these metals in a consumer air product, and HMTc does not manufacture one: no occupational exposure limit and no ambient- or indoor-air guideline is converted into a product ceiling anywhere in this category. Because this form works by passive evaporation at room temperature, the emitting mass concentrates its non-volatile content as it depletes, so a result on a fresh unit is a lower bound on the concentration present in the same unit at end of life. ROUTING. Placement in this category follows the taxonomy boundary rules: the primary exposure pathway must be inhalation or ambient-air emission; an essential oil sold as aromatherapy for diffusion routes here, the same oil sold as a topical leave-on skin product routes to Category 13 and sold as a dietary supplement routes to Category 16; and marketing and positioning decide routing where one formulation could serve several functions.
material: the additive as supplied (carrier granule, bead, powder or pad substrate with its fragrance load, dye and flow agents), drawn into and dispersed by an appliance airstream
components: The component-level sampling plan for this row covers the carrier granule, bead, powder or pad substrate (mineral, zeolite, cellulose, starch or polymer); the fragrance load; the dye; any anti-caking, free-flow or fixative agent; and the sachet, disc backing or dispenser body. Every listed component is sampled and tested as a distinct component by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, and hexavalent-chromium reflex speciation on a component follows the reference method published on this row's Cr-VI cell. Beyond the components, the friable fines fraction is separated and analysed in its own right, the published value applying to it directly. EMISSION PATH. The components in the emission path, which branch (b) of every numeric cell's disposition governs, are the carrier granule, bead, powder or pad substrate, and the sachet, disc backing or dispenser body through which the additive is drawn into the appliance airstream. Every component result carries a criterion and a lot consequence under the three ordered branches published on each numeric cell: a sovereign instrument that reaches the component and the analyte governs it in its own basis and an exceedance blocks certification; an emission-path component is governed through the published value applied to emitting material sampled from the finished assembled article; and any remaining component result is held to ALARA against demonstrated process capability, with CAPA, raw-material traceback and a block on certification where an uncontrolled source is confirmed. No component ceiling is invented.
basis_guard_note: Category 22 numeric cells are anchored ONLY in route-scoped inhaled-product content instruments, whose register basis strings are "product as tested" (Colorado, Maryland) and "cannabis or cannabis product" (California). The guard admits exactly those and rejects, by construction, every other basis family the register carries: dietary wet-weight maximum levels (an ingestion basis), food-contact and toy element-migration limits (a leachate basis), RoHS and REACH percent-by-weight restrictions on homogeneous materials, plastics, paints and batteries (an end-of-life materials basis), surface-coating dried-film limits, drinking-water statutory limits (a per-litre basis), cosmetic technically-avoidable trace limits (a dermal basis), colour-additive purity specifications, feed 12-percent-moisture bases, and the candlewick prohibition threshold, which is expressed on the mass of the metal in the wick core and not on any product. A number in the wrong basis is not a maximum level for this product form and must never anchor a row here.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only initial setting: the strictest applicable sovereign maximum for this exact product form in its native basis; disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated; control where neither a sovereign number nor a supportable near-neighbour analogue exists; never occurrence-derived)

Pb.basis: as sold, ug of element per kg of the emitting material (product as tested)
Pb.source_scope: inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray
Pb.label: read-across from the Colorado Marijuana Enforcement Division route-scoped maximum for inhaled product and metered-dose nasal spray (500 ug/kg), corroborated at the identical value by California DCC section 15723 for inhalable products
Pb.substantiation: No government anywhere sets a lead content maximum for an air freshener, plug-in evaporator, puff releaser, candle body, wax melt, oil or nebula diffuser, gel or reed diffuser, incense stick, potpourri, vacuum-cleaner fragrance additive or fragrance refill. The only sovereign heavy-metal instrument in any jurisdiction that names a product in this category is the United States CPSC prohibition on lead-cored candlewicks, 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13), mirrored by Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956; it restricts lead in the metal of a wick core and covers no other analyte and no other product form. The cell is therefore a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS, and it is taken on the axis the regulators themselves used: route of administration. Colorado's 2022 heavy-metal table and Maryland's Technical Authority Rev. 6.0 both publish a route LADDER over the same underlying matrices, with the inhalation row strictest, the oral row looser and the topical or cutaneous row looser still. The value is therefore a function of the route, not of the source matrix's chemistry, and Colorado scopes its strictest row in the instrument's own words to "inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray", which describes a delivery mechanism this category shares. Maryland's own route gap is the sharpest available evidence for that reading: its inhalation-route total-chromium value is 600 ug/kg while its oral and cutaneous values for the same products are 1,100,000 ug/kg. Selected value 500 ug/kg, from Colorado (co2022 inhaled/nasal row). California DCC section 15723 independently sets the identical 0.5 ug/g for inhalable products (us_ca_dcc_2026_pb_inhalable_cannabis_0_5ugg), so two sub-national regulators converge on this value. The looser or route-unspecific values on the register are recorded and NOT selected: Maryland inhalation route 1000 ug/kg, Massachusetts all-uses protocol 500 ug/kg (equal but route-unspecific), Nevada 1200 ug/kg, Israel IMC-GMP Procedure 152 5000 ug/kg. The basis is identical to this row's native basis, micrograms of element per kilogram of product as tested, so no basis conversion, no reconstitution and no dry-to-wet adjustment is performed. The read-across is published as `read-across` and never as `regulatory-alignment`, because no instrument regulates this exact cell. Adopting it tightens rather than relaxes the applicable regulatory position: it is three to four orders of magnitude stricter than every article-content instrument that actually binds these products (RoHS lead at 1,000,000 ug/kg of homogeneous material, the candlewick-core prohibition threshold at 600,000 ug/kg of wick-core metal, REACH cadmium in polymers at 100,000 ug/kg). No occurrence, percentile, feasibility or precautionary input touched the number in either direction. Determined on the additive as supplied, homogenised across the retail unit, with the friable fines fraction analysed separately by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS with collision/reaction-cell control of the interfered masses, with the article's non-emitting components digested and screened separately per this row's component plan. DISPOSITION OF THE ADDITIONAL ANALYSES THIS CELL MANDATES. This cell requires two analyses beyond the published test, and each carries a criterion and a lot consequence, so that no mandatory analysis on this row is an obligation without an outcome. COMPONENT RESULTS, THE FIRST ADDITIONAL ANALYSIS THIS CELL MANDATES. The published ceiling of 500 ug/kg governs the emitting material and is NOT transferred to a component's bulk content: a mineral or zeolite carrier substrate, a metal-bearing dye or anti-caking agent, or a pigmented dispenser body is or may be substantially metal, metal-plated, metal-glazed or metal-pigmented by construction, and reading an emitting-material value against a structural component's bulk content would be exactly the basis conflation this row's basis guard exists to prevent, failing every compliant article for a metal that never enters the air. Every component result is instead dispositioned in three ordered branches, and no component result is left outside them. (a) WHERE A SOVEREIGN INSTRUMENT REACHES THE COMPONENT AND THIS ANALYTE, that instrument is the criterion. For lead and this row's components, branch (a) is EMPTY, and the instruments checked before saying so are named rather than waved at: EU RoHS 2011/65/EU is scoped to the homogeneous materials of electrical and electronic equipment and this row carries no powered sub-assembly; Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 on batteries is scoped to batteries and this row contains none; REACH Annex XVII entry 63 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2015/628 (eu_2015_628_pb_mouthable_general_public_articles_0_05pct) reaches only articles supplied to the general public that may be placed in the mouth by children; Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 reaches consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles and does not reach a packaging, sachet or decorative textile that is not worn; the EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC with EN 71-3, the CPSIA surface-coating limit and the Canadian and Australian toy-coating limits reach accessible toy material and toy surface coatings, and none of these articles is a toy; 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13) reaches only the metal of a candlewick core and this row has no wick core; the food-contact ceramic, glassware and enamelware instruments reach only articles intended to come into contact with food. Every component result on this row therefore falls to branch (b) or branch (c), and neither leaves a result without a criterion or without a lot consequence. (b) WHERE THE COMPONENT IS IN THE EMISSION PATH (the carrier granule, bead, powder or pad substrate, and the sachet, disc backing or dispenser body through which the additive is drawn into the appliance airstream), the criterion is the published ceiling itself, applied where its basis makes it meaningful: the test is performed on emitting material sampled from the finished, filled and assembled article rather than from a pre-fill bulk batch, at the end of the declared shelf life at the declared storage conditions, with the sample homogenised across the retail unit, so that any lead transferred out of an emission-path component into the emitting material is carried into the published result rather than escaping it. An emitting-material result at or above 500 ug/kg fails the lot. A rising component result while the emitting material stays below the ceiling does not by itself fail the lot and falls to branch (c). (c) OTHERWISE, for a component outside the emission path that no sovereign instrument reaches for lead, the component result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule, in the same terms this row's control cells already use: the result is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the carrier-substrate supplier, the fragrance house, the dye supplier, the anti-caking and fixative supplier and the sachet, backing or dispenser converter; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row. No component ceiling is invented in branch (c), because no credible sovereign government publishes a lead content maximum for these components in this product form, and an occupational exposure limit, an indoor-air guideline and an ambient-air standard are none of them converted into one. FRIABLE FINES FRACTION, THE SECOND ADDITIONAL ANALYSIS THIS CELL MANDATES. The friable fines fraction is not a separate matrix requiring a separate criterion: it is this row's emitting material in its most respirable form, and the published ceiling of 500 ug/kg applies to it directly and on its own terms. A fines-fraction result at or above 500 ug/kg fails the lot independently of the bulk result, and the bulk result never averages the fines away. Where the fines fraction and the bulk result diverge by more than the combined expanded uncertainty of the two determinations, the lot is held, re-sampled after reconditioning to the declared particle-size distribution and re-tested, and a confirmed enrichment of lead into the respirable fraction that the manufacturer cannot attribute to a controlled source blocks certification. The fines result is otherwise dispositioned under the control-and-escalation rule stated above. No emission-rate limit, per-actuation dose limit or indoor-air concentration limit is published for this row, because no credible sovereign government sets one for any product in this category and none is manufactured from an occupational or ambient-air value.

iAs.rationale: iAs carries no product-specific sovereign cell; it is a component of and bounded by its parent total tAs (iAs <= tAs), an enforceable ceiling via reflex speciation rather than an empty cell.
iAs.reference_method: iAs speciation reflexed when the parent total reaches min(species limit, 50 percent of the parent-total limit); the species never substitutes for the parent-total report.

tHg.source_scope: inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray
tHg.label: read-across from the Colorado Marijuana Enforcement Division route-scoped maximum for inhaled product and metered-dose nasal spray (100 ug/kg), corroborated at the identical value by California DCC section 15723 for inhalable products
tHg.substantiation: No government anywhere sets a total mercury content maximum for an air freshener, plug-in evaporator, puff releaser, candle body, wax melt, oil or nebula diffuser, gel or reed diffuser, incense stick, potpourri, vacuum-cleaner fragrance additive or fragrance refill. The only sovereign heavy-metal instrument in any jurisdiction that names a product in this category is the United States CPSC prohibition on lead-cored candlewicks, 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13), mirrored by Australia's Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956; it restricts lead in the metal of a wick core and covers no other analyte and no other product form. The cell is therefore a DISCLOSED READ-ACROSS, and it is taken on the axis the regulators themselves used: route of administration. Colorado's 2022 heavy-metal table and Maryland's Technical Authority Rev. 6.0 both publish a route LADDER over the same underlying matrices, with the inhalation row strictest, the oral row looser and the topical or cutaneous row looser still. The value is therefore a function of the route, not of the source matrix's chemistry, and Colorado scopes its strictest row in the instrument's own words to "inhaled product or audited product administered by metered-dose nasal spray", which describes a delivery mechanism this category shares. Maryland's own route gap is the sharpest available evidence for that reading: its inhalation-route total-chromium value is 600 ug/kg while its oral and cutaneous values for the same products are 1,100,000 ug/kg. Selected value 100 ug/kg, from Colorado (co2022 inhaled/nasal row). California DCC section 15723 independently sets the identical 0.1 ug/g for inhalable products (us_ca_dcc_2026_thg_inhalable_cannabis_0_1ugg); California's own non-inhalable value for the same products is 3000 ug/kg, thirty times looser. The looser or route-unspecific values on the register are recorded and NOT selected: Maryland inhalation route 200 ug/kg, Massachusetts all-uses protocol 500 ug/kg, Nevada 400 ug/kg; Israel IMC-GMP Procedure 152 sits at 100 ug/kg, equal to the selected value, and California DCC section 15723 also sits at 100 ug/kg. The basis is identical to this row's native basis, micrograms of element per kilogram of product as tested, so no basis conversion, no reconstitution and no dry-to-wet adjustment is performed. The read-across is published as `read-across` and never as `regulatory-alignment`, because no instrument regulates this exact cell. Adopting it tightens rather than relaxes the applicable regulatory position: it is three to four orders of magnitude stricter than every article-content instrument that actually binds these products (RoHS lead at 1,000,000 ug/kg of homogeneous material, the candlewick-core prohibition threshold at 600,000 ug/kg of wick-core metal, REACH cadmium in polymers at 100,000 ug/kg). No occurrence, percentile, feasibility or precautionary input touched the number in either direction. Determined on the additive as supplied, homogenised across the retail unit, with the friable fines fraction analysed separately by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS with collision/reaction-cell control of the interfered masses, with the article's non-emitting components digested and screened separately per this row's component plan. DISPOSITION OF THE ADDITIONAL ANALYSES THIS CELL MANDATES. This cell requires two analyses beyond the published test, and each carries a criterion and a lot consequence, so that no mandatory analysis on this row is an obligation without an outcome. COMPONENT RESULTS, THE FIRST ADDITIONAL ANALYSIS THIS CELL MANDATES. The published ceiling of 100 ug/kg governs the emitting material and is NOT transferred to a component's bulk content: a mineral or zeolite carrier substrate, a metal-bearing dye or anti-caking agent, or a pigmented dispenser body is or may be substantially metal, metal-plated, metal-glazed or metal-pigmented by construction, and reading an emitting-material value against a structural component's bulk content would be exactly the basis conflation this row's basis guard exists to prevent, failing every compliant article for a metal that never enters the air. Every component result is instead dispositioned in three ordered branches, and no component result is left outside them. (a) WHERE A SOVEREIGN INSTRUMENT REACHES THE COMPONENT AND THIS ANALYTE, that instrument is the criterion. For total mercury and this row's components, branch (a) is EMPTY, and the instruments checked before saying so are named rather than waved at: EU RoHS 2011/65/EU is scoped to the homogeneous materials of electrical and electronic equipment and this row carries no powered sub-assembly; Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 on batteries is scoped to batteries and this row contains none; REACH Annex XVII entry 63 as amended by Regulation (EU) 2015/628 (eu_2015_628_pb_mouthable_general_public_articles_0_05pct) reaches only articles supplied to the general public that may be placed in the mouth by children; Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 reaches consumer clothing and skin-contact textiles and does not reach a packaging, sachet or decorative textile that is not worn; the EU Toy Safety Directive 2009/48/EC with EN 71-3, the CPSIA surface-coating limit and the Canadian and Australian toy-coating limits reach accessible toy material and toy surface coatings, and none of these articles is a toy; 16 CFR 1500.17(a)(13) reaches only the metal of a candlewick core and this row has no wick core; the food-contact ceramic, glassware and enamelware instruments reach only articles intended to come into contact with food. Every component result on this row therefore falls to branch (b) or branch (c), and neither leaves a result without a criterion or without a lot consequence. (b) WHERE THE COMPONENT IS IN THE EMISSION PATH (the carrier granule, bead, powder or pad substrate, and the sachet, disc backing or dispenser body through which the additive is drawn into the appliance airstream), the criterion is the published ceiling itself, applied where its basis makes it meaningful: the test is performed on emitting material sampled from the finished, filled and assembled article rather than from a pre-fill bulk batch, at the end of the declared shelf life at the declared storage conditions, with the sample homogenised across the retail unit, so that any mercury transferred out of an emission-path component into the emitting material is carried into the published result rather than escaping it. An emitting-material result at or above 100 ug/kg fails the lot. A rising component result while the emitting material stays below the ceiling does not by itself fail the lot and falls to branch (c). (c) OTHERWISE, for a component outside the emission path that no sovereign instrument reaches for total mercury, the component result is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule, in the same terms this row's control cells already use: the result is held to ALARA against the manufacturer's demonstrated process capability for that formulation and component set; a result outside that capability band, or an unexplained step change between lots, triggers CAPA and raw-material traceback to the carrier-substrate supplier, the fragrance house, the dye supplier, the anti-caking and fixative supplier and the sachet, backing or dispenser converter; a confirmed uncontrolled source blocks certification until it is removed or substituted; and the analyte goes onto priority surveillance for this row. No component ceiling is invented in branch (c), because no credible sovereign government publishes a total-mercury content maximum for these components in this product form, and an occupational exposure limit, an indoor-air guideline and an ambient-air standard are none of them converted into one. FRIABLE FINES FRACTION, THE SECOND ADDITIONAL ANALYSIS THIS CELL MANDATES. The friable fines fraction is not a separate matrix requiring a separate criterion: it is this row's emitting material in its most respirable form, and the published ceiling of 100 ug/kg applies to it directly and on its own terms. A fines-fraction result at or above 100 ug/kg fails the lot independently of the bulk result, and the bulk result never averages the fines away. Where the fines fraction and the bulk result diverge by more than the combined expanded uncertainty of the two determinations, the lot is held, re-sampled after reconditioning to the declared particle-size distribution and re-tested, and a confirmed enrichment of mercury into the respirable fraction that the manufacturer cannot attribute to a controlled source blocks certification. The fines result is otherwise dispositioned under the control-and-escalation rule stated above. No emission-rate limit, per-actuation dose limit or indoor-air concentration limit is published for this row, because no credible sovereign government sets one for any product in this category and none is manufactured from an occupational or ambient-air value.

MeHg.rationale: MeHg carries no product-specific sovereign cell; it is a component of and bounded by its parent total tHg (MeHg <= tHg), an enforceable ceiling via reflex speciation rather than an empty cell.
MeHg.reference_method: MeHg speciation reflexed when the parent total reaches min(species limit, 50 percent of the parent-total limit); the species never substitutes for the parent-total report.

Cr.screen_note: Total chromium is not the health-relevant analyte. It is dominated by trivalent chromium, an essential trace element, while the species of concern by the inhalation route is hexavalent chromium, a Group 1 respiratory carcinogen. The Maryland inhalation-route value is a real sovereign number in the right basis and is published here, but it is recorded as a SCREEN: it is the tripwire that triggers hexavalent-chromium speciation (see the Cr-VI cell), not a standalone protective ceiling, and it is excluded from the firm-limit count. Total chromium is never satisfied by a hexavalent-chromium result and hexavalent chromium is never satisfied by a total-chromium result.
